author: Thomas à Kempis
title: That the Grace of God doth not join itself to those who mind earthly things

verses.text: “My Son, precious is My grace, it suffereth not itself to be joined with outward things, nor with earthly consolations.
verses.modernizedText: “My Son, My grace is precious; it does not allow itself to be joined with outward things or earthly consolations.

verses.text: Therefore thou oughtest to cast away all things which hinder grace, if thou longest to receive the inpouring thereof.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore you ought to cast away everything that hinders grace if you long to receive its outpouring.

verses.text: Seek a secret place for thyself, love to dwell alone with thyself, desire the conversation of no one; but rather pour out thy devout prayer to God, that thou mayest possess a contrite mind and a pure conscience.
verses.modernizedText: Seek a secret place for yourself, love to dwell alone with yourself, and desire no one’s conversation; instead pour out your devout prayer to God, so that you may possess a contrite mind and a pure conscience.

verses.text: Count the whole world as nought; seek to be alone with God before all outward things.
verses.modernizedText: Count the whole world as nothing; seek solitude with God before all outward things.

verses.text: For thou canst not be alone with Me, and at the same time be delighted with transitory things.
verses.modernizedText: For you cannot be alone with Me and at the same time delight in passing things.

verses.text: Thou oughtest to be separated from thy acquaintances and dear friends, and keep thy mind free from all worldly comfort.
verses.modernizedText: You ought to be separated from your acquaintances and dear friends, and keep your mind free from all worldly comfort.

verses.text: So the blessed Apostle Peter beseecheth, that Christ’s faithful ones bear themselves in this world as strangers and pilgrims.(1)
verses.modernizedText: So the blessed Apostle Peter urges Christ’s faithful ones to conduct themselves in this world as strangers and pilgrims.(1)

verses.text: “Oh how great a confidence shall there be to the dying man whom no affection to anything detaineth in the world?
verses.modernizedText: “Oh, how great will be the confidence of the dying person whom no affection for anything holds in the world!

verses.text: But to have a heart so separated from all things, a sickly soul doth not yet comprehend, nor doth the carnal man know the liberty of the spiritual man.
verses.modernizedText: But a sickly soul does not yet understand having a heart so separated from all things, nor does the carnal person know the freedom of the spiritual person.

verses.text: But if indeed he desire to be spiritually minded, he must renounce both those who are far off, and those who are near, and to beware of no man more than himself.
verses.modernizedText: But if he truly desires to be spiritually minded, he must renounce both those who are far off and those who are near, and beware of no one more than himself.

verses.text: If thou perfectly conquer thyself, very easily shalt thou subdue all things besides.
verses.modernizedText: If you perfectly conquer yourself, you will very easily subdue all other things.

verses.text: Perfect victory is the triumph over oneself.
verses.modernizedText: Perfect victory is triumph over oneself.

verses.text: For whoso keepeth himself in subjection, in such manner that the sensual affections obey the reason, and the reason in all things obeyeth Me, he truly is conqueror of himself, and lord of the world.
verses.modernizedText: For whoever keeps himself in subjection, so that his sensual affections obey reason and reason obeys Me in all things, truly conquers himself and is lord of the world.

verses.text: “If thou desire to climb to this height, thou oughtest to start bravely, and to lay the axe to the root, to the end that thou mayest pull up and destroy the hidden inordinate inclination towards thyself, and towards all selfish and earthly good.
verses.modernizedText: “If you desire to climb to this height, you ought to begin bravely and lay the axe to the root, so that you may pull up and destroy the hidden, excessive inclination toward yourself and toward all selfish and earthly good.

verses.text: From this sin, that a man loveth himself too inordinately, almost everything hangeth which needeth to be utterly overcome: when that evil is conquered and put under foot, there shall be great peace and tranquillity continually.
verses.modernizedText: Almost everything that needs to be utterly overcome depends on this sin, that a person loves himself too excessively; when that evil is conquered and put underfoot, there will be great peace and tranquility continually.

verses.text: But because few strive earnestly to die perfectly to themselves, and do not heartily go forth from themselves, therefore do they remain entangled in themselves, and cannot be raised in spirit above themselves.
verses.modernizedText: But because few strive earnestly to die perfectly to themselves and do not go forth from themselves wholeheartedly, they remain entangled in themselves and cannot be raised in spirit above themselves.

verses.text: But he who desireth to walk at liberty with Me, must of necessity mortify all his evil and inordinate affections, and must cling to no creature with selfish love.”
verses.modernizedText: But whoever desires to walk at liberty with Me must mortify all his evil and excessive affections and must cling to no creature with selfish love.”
